transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-10-18
Time: 10:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Sarah Gomez (Evergreen CTO), Rajiv Singh (Evergreen ML Eng Lead), Emily Park (Evergreen Data Eng)

Summary:
Quick discovery call focused on Evergreen's plan to move production LLM workloads off OpenAI into a Dedicated/Private deployment. Key concerns: eval parity with OpenAI, integration friction for current APIs (function-calling), latency and cost for high-volume inference, VPC/KMS requirements, and migration runbook.

Topics:
- Current stack (OpenAI + some self-hosted vLLM for on-prem experiments)
- Compatibility considerations (API parity, prompt/eval regression)
- Dedicated vs Private (VPC) tradeoffs and SLAs
- Benchmarks and migration plan
- Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logging

Action items (from call) - see metadata for owners/dates

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll kick off in a sec. Quick intros?
[00:10] Sarah Gomez: Hi, Sarah Gomez here, CTO at Evergreen. Thanks Maya.
[00:15] Rajiv Singh: Rajiv, ML eng lead. We run most inference on OpenAI right now, and experimenting with vLLM self-hosted for a few private datasets.
[00:25] Emily Park: Emily, data eng, I'll help with traffic numbers and infra questions.
[00:30] Maya Patel: Great. Liam, you want to give a quick technical intro?
[00:35] Liam Chen: Yeah, sure. I'm Liam, SE on the Redwood side. We focus on inference runtimes, batching, KV cache, um kv cache, sorry K-V cache management, and routing across hosted/dedicated/private.
[01:05] Sarah Gomez: Awesome. Our primary ask — cost and latency. We have a high-volume summarization pipeline, roughly 300M tokens/month currently to OpenAI, peaks at, uh, 15 req/s with variable context lengths up to 8k tokens. Latency matters for our interactive flows.
[01:40] Rajiv Singh: And importantly, our eval suite -- we track hallucination/regression across ~1500 prom sets. We can't have a drop in quality when we move.
[02:05] Maya Patel: Totally. That's a common concern. Two areas to discuss: functional parity (function-calling, chat-format, streaming) and eval parity — we recommend running parallel evals and a benchmark harness.
[02:35] Emily Park: On the infra side, we need VPC peering or private deployment — some data never leaves our network. Is Redwood Private fully air-gapped?
[02:50] Liam Chen: We offer a Private deployment with a customer-managed control plane option, and on-prem packages where necessary. For VPC we do peering and dedicated tunnels, and you can integrate KMS/HSM for key control.
[03:20] Sarah Gomez: And certifications? SOC2?
[03:25] Maya Patel: Yes, SOC 2 Type II, and we have documentation for ISO and penetration testing results. I'll share the whitepaper after the call.
[03:45] Rajiv Singh: On models — we currently use gpt-4 style OpenAI endpoints and some Anthropic for assistant-style tasks. If we move to Redwood Dedicated, how compatible is the API? Do we need to rewrite calls?
[04:10] Liam Chen: API compatibility is high — Redwood supports a REST/SDK interface for chat, completion, embeddings, and function/tool calling. There are small differences in model names and parameters, but in practice it's a straightforward swap for most apps. We'd recommend a pilot to validate function-calling parity.
[04:40] Sarah Gomez: What about the runtime differences? We saw some variance when we tried vLLM with our prompts — sometimes lower perf.
[04:55] Liam Chen: Right, vLLM and TGI have different kernel stacks. Redwood's serving runtime includes kernel selection, quantization-aware execution, and continuous batching which aims to match or beat OpenAI latencies for similar models. We'll run your prompts to validate.
[05:25] Rajiv Singh: Can you do exact-match evals? We need to know tokenization and sampling parity to ensure outputs don't drift.
[05:40] Liam Chen: Yes, we run exact-regression tests using the same seed/sampling config where possible; for non-deterministic decoders we recommend an ensemble of evals and monitoring. We'll provide the harness so you can run both sides.
[06:10] Emily Park: For throughput, are you recommending Dedicated reserved capacity or Private?
[06:20] Maya Patel: For your volume, reserved Dedicated capacity (SLA-backed) usually hits the sweet spot — predictable throughput and lower per-token cost vs hosted usage. Private is for the cases where data residency or air-gap is required.
[06:40] Sarah Gomez: Pricing concern: how much savings can we expect vs OpenAI?
[06:50] Maya Patel: It varies by model and batching. We typically see 20-50% unit-cost savings at scale with Dedicated due to better batching, KV caching, and quantization options. We'll send a model-by-model estimate as an example.
[07:20] Rajiv Singh: About caching — our prompt patterns are heavy on prefixes, will Redwood's prefix caching help?
[07:30] Liam Chen: Yes, prefix and KV caching are first-class. We also do workload-aware batching — the net effect is a big reduction in per-token compute for stable prefixes.
[07:50] Sarah Gomez: Any gotchas migrating existing function-calling integrations? We use nested function calls and streaming responses for UX.
[08:00] Liam Chen: We support streaming and function/tool calling. Complex nested functions sometimes require small adjustments — e.g., handling chunked tool outputs — but our SDKs provide helpers. In the pilot we'll test your exact flows.
[08:30] Rajiv Singh: What about quantized models? We saw odd tokenization differences in 4-bit runs.
[08:40] Liam Chen: Quantization can affect deterministic exact-match outputs, especially if you're relying on low-temp greedy outputs. We'll run both float and quantized variants to surface any regressions.
[09:05] Sarah Gomez: Security: can we use our KMS?
[09:10] Maya Patel: Yes, in Dedicated/Private you can integrate your KMS/HSM. For hosted, we offer safeguards but not customer-managed keys.
[09:25] Emily Park: Audit logs — we need token-level logs for a short retention window and aggregate metrics for longer.
[09:35] Liam Chen: The Console supports per-token cost/latency breakdowns and audit logging. Retention windows are configurable as an add-on.
[09:55] Sarah Gomez: Okay. On the migration timeline: we ideally want a pilot in Q4, production in Q1. Is that feasible?
[10:05] Maya Patel: Yes, pilot in 2-4 weeks depending on your readiness. We'll size the reserved capacity and run the benchmark in parallel.
[10:20] Rajiv Singh: One more — are there network egress considerations? If we do Dedicated in a cloud region, will traffic between our services and the cluster be routed without public internet?
[10:35] Liam Chen: For Dedicated we can colocate in your VPC or use private peering; that avoids public egress. For hosted it's over TLS to Redwood endpoints.
[10:50] Sarah Gomez: Any notes about compatibility with our current embedding pipelines? We use OpenAI embeddings for vector search.
[11:00] Liam Chen: Redwood supports embeddings and you can either use our embedding endpoints or run private embeddings in Dedicated. We'll compare vector quality as part of the evals.
[11:20] Emily Park: On staffing — what support levels do you provide for migration?
[11:25] Maya Patel: We provide a solutions engineer-led onboarding for Dedicated, with runbook, 2-week ramp support, and optional SRE concierge for the Private deployment.
[11:40] Rajiv Singh: Competitors: we also evaluated Anthropic and Azure managed endpoints. Any differentiator?
[11:50] Maya Patel: Our focus is production economics and predictable latency across environments. Unlike generic cloud endpoints, we surface cost/latency levers and provide a unified runtime for hosted/dedicated/private.
[12:10] Sarah Gomez: Ok that's helpful.
[12:15] --- brief cross talk while scheduling ---
[12:40] Maya Patel: To recap: Redwood to run 3-benchmark suite, share security/cert docs, send pricing, and schedule SE deep-dive. Evergreen to share prompt set, traffic profile, and success criteria.
[13:00] Sarah Gomez: Yup. We'll get that over by Tuesday.
[13:05] Rajiv Singh: Quick Q — how do you handle model rollbacks if a release causes regressions?
[13:15] Liam Chen: We do canary rollouts, A/B comparisons, and automatic fallback policies to previous model versions if metrics degrade.
[13:30] Emily Park: Great. One final small ask: will you provide a sample SLO doc for latency under the reserved capacity?
[13:40] Maya Patel: Yes, we'll include an SLO appendix in the SOW draft.
[13:50] Sarah Gomez: Thanks all.
[13:55] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[14:00] Meeting ended

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (K-V cache vs KV cache), filler words and overlap present. Some speaker labels generalized.
